answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by letting trust accumulate through a long history of verified useful work, so a new identity starts with tiny limits no matter how many copies appear at once. Like a sparrow that must return season after season before it is trusted near the nest, an agent earns larger duties gradually, each honest job adding a small ember to its record while failures cool it down. Reputation grown timber by timber over time cannot be bought, so waiting defeats mass forgery.
